title: Cohen power series full parameter coordinates
statement: Let Lambda be a Cohen ring with prime uniformizer p and let S=Lambda[[X_1,...,X_n]]. Let t be an ordered list of n elements of S such that C(p)::t is a regular system of parameters. Then there is a Lambda-algebra equivalence Lambda[[Y_1,...,Y_length(t)]] -> S which sends Y_i to the ith entry of t. The power-series and parameter-system notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Cohen rings are [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM (3) and its proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NM

proof.text: Apply the proved regular-complete power-series theorem to obtain completeness, domain structure, dimension n+1 and the maximal-ideal presentation. Every entry of t belongs to the maximal ideal. The complete universal property supplies a ring endomorphism f fixing constants and sending variables to t, indexed via the given length equality.

The source maximal ideal maps onto itself. If the regular-complete presentation has prime p′, the ideals (p′) and (p) both equal the coefficient maximal ideal; map their equality along C. Constants are fixed and variables go to t, so the image of the presented maximal ideal is the ideal generated by C(p) and t, namely the maximal ideal.

The constant-coefficient kernel calculation places the difference between a series and its constant in the variables ideal, hence in the maximal ideal. Thus the residue map composed with f is surjective. Apply Mathlib surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective to conclude f is surjective. If a nonzero g is in its kernel, domain structure makes g a nonzero divisor. Mathlib ringKrullDim_succ_le_of_surjective then gives (n+1)+1 <= n+1, impossible for finite n. Thus f is injective. Its constant values provide algebra compatibility; AlgEquiv.ofBijective and renameEquiv along the length equality give the stated equivalence and variable values. All operations cover the empty list and zero variables.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07NM (3); Q1 implements full coordinates by complete universal property, successive approximation and the finite-dimensional domain kernel argument instead of associated-graded inversion.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_full_parameters_cohen
    (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [IsLocalRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (p n : ℕ) (hΛ : IsCohenRing p Λ) (t : List (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
    (hparams : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (C (p : Λ) :: t))
    (hlen : t.length = n) :
    ∃ e : MvPowerSeries (Fin t.length) Λ ≃ₐ[Λ] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ,
      ∀ i : Fin t.length, e (X i) = t.get i
